request: how do you simplify the ratio 12:18?

beats.intent: 12 red counters in two rows and 18 blue counters in three rows
beats.narration: A bag has twelve red counters and eighteen blue: a ratio of twelve to eighteen.
beats.code:
stage.title("Simplifying 12 : 18")
red = VGroup(*[Dot([-5.8 + 0.45 * i, 1.6 - 0.5 * j, 0], radius=0.15, color=RED) for j in range(2) for i in range(6)])
blue = VGroup(*[Dot([-5.8 + 0.45 * i, -0.2 - 0.5 * j, 0], radius=0.15, color=BLUE) for j in range(3) for i in range(6)])
stage.play(FadeIn(red), FadeIn(blue))
stage.add(red, blue)
stage.label(red, "12", direction=LEFT, color=RED)
stage.label(blue, "18", direction=LEFT, color=BLUE)

beats.intent: Each row of 6 boxed: 2 groups of red, 3 groups of blue
beats.narration: Both numbers split into groups of six: twelve is two sixes and eighteen is three sixes.
beats.code:
rows = VGroup(*[SurroundingRectangle(VGroup(*red[6 * j:6 * j + 6]), color=YELLOW, buff=0.08) for j in range(2)], *[SurroundingRectangle(VGroup(*blue[6 * j:6 * j + 6]), color=YELLOW, buff=0.08) for j in range(3)])
stage.play(Create(rows))
stage.add(rows)
stage.label(rows, "groups of 6", direction=RIGHT, color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: Each group of six shrunk to one block: 2 red blocks and 3 blue blocks
beats.narration: Replace each group of six by a single block: two red blocks and three blue. The proportions haven't changed.
beats.code:
rb = VGroup(*[Square(0.45, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.7) for _ in range(2)]).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.05).move_to([-0.6, 1.35, 0])
bb = VGroup(*[Square(0.45, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.7) for _ in range(3)]).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.05).move_to([-0.6, -0.7, 0])
stage.play(TransformFromCopy(VGroup(*rows[:2]), rb), TransformFromCopy(VGroup(*rows[2:]), bb), run_time=1.3)
stage.add(rb, bb)
stage.label(bb, "2 : 3", direction=DOWN, color=GREEN)

beats.intent: The counters beside 12 : 18 = 2 : 3, dividing both by 6
beats.narration: Divide both sides by six, their highest common factor: twelve to eighteen simplifies to two to three.

request: why are 2/3, 4/6 and 8/12 the same fraction?

beats.intent: A bar cut into thirds with two shaded: 2/3
beats.narration: Shade two thirds of a bar.
beats.code:
stage.title("Equivalent fractions")
w = 6
x0 = -6
bar = lambda n, k, y: VGroup(*[Rectangle(width=w / n, height=0.6, color=WHITE, fill_color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.7 if i < k else 0) for i in range(n)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0).move_to([x0 + w / 2, y, 0])
b3 = bar(3, 2, 1.6)
stage.play(FadeIn(b3))
stage.add(b3)
stage.label(b3, "2/3", direction=RIGHT, color=BLUE)

beats.intent: The same bar with each third cut in half: 4 of 6 shaded
beats.narration: Cut every third in half. There are now six pieces and four are shaded, but the shaded length is the same.
beats.code:
b6 = bar(6, 4, 0.4)
stage.play(TransformFromCopy(b3, b6))
stage.add(b6)
stage.label(b6, "4/6", direction=RIGHT, color=BLUE)

beats.intent: Cut again into twelfths: 8 of 12 shaded, the shaded edge lined up across all three bars
beats.narration: Cut each piece in half again: eight of twelve. A dashed line shows the shaded part ends in the same place every time.
beats.code:
b12 = bar(12, 8, -0.8)
stage.play(TransformFromCopy(b6, b12))
stage.add(b12)
stage.label(b12, "8/12", direction=RIGHT, color=BLUE)
edge = DashedLine([x0 + w * 2 / 3, 2.1, 0], [x0 + w * 2 / 3, -1.3, 0], color=YELLOW)
stage.play(Create(edge))
stage.add(edge)

beats.intent: The bars beside 2/3 = 4/6 = 8/12, top and bottom multiplied by the same number
beats.narration: Doubling the pieces doubles both the top and the bottom. Multiply top and bottom by the same number and the fraction doesn't change.

request: why do a heavy ball and a light ball hit the ground at the same time?

beats.intent: A 20 m tower with a 10 kg ball and a 1 kg ball side by side at the top
beats.narration: Drop a ten kilogram ball and a one kilogram ball from a twenty metre tower, with no air to slow them.
beats.code:
stage.title("Heavy and light, falling")
k = 0.25
ground = Line([-6.5, -2.5, 0], [0.5, -2.5, 0], color=GREY_B)
tower = Rectangle(width=1.0, height=20 * k, color=GREY_B, fill_opacity=0.3).move_to([-5.9, -2.5 + 10 * k, 0])
heavy = Circle(radius=0.35, color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=0.9).move_to([-3.8, 2.5, 0])
light = Circle(radius=0.15, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.9).move_to([-2.6, 2.5, 0])
stage.play(Create(ground), FadeIn(tower), FadeIn(heavy), FadeIn(light))
stage.add(ground, tower, heavy, light)
stage.label(heavy, "10 kg", direction=LEFT, color=ORANGE)
stage.label(light, "1 kg", direction=RIGHT, color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: Both balls falling, ghost images at 1 s and 2 s at the same heights; both land at 2 s
beats.narration: Let go. After one second both have fallen five metres; after two seconds both hit the ground together.
beats.code:
marks = VGroup()
for t in (1, 2):
    y = 2.5 - 5 * t * t * k
    marks.add(DashedLine([-4.5, y, 0], [-1.6, y, 0], color=GREY_B), Text(f"{t} s", font_size=24).move_to([-0.8, y + (0.25 if t == 2 else 0), 0]))
    stage.add(heavy.copy().set_opacity(0.3).move_to([-3.8, y if t == 1 else -2.15, 0]), light.copy().set_opacity(0.3).move_to([-2.6, y if t == 1 else -2.35, 0]))
stage.play(heavy.animate.move_to([-3.8, -2.15, 0]), light.animate.move_to([-2.6, -2.35, 0]), rate_func=rate_functions.ease_in_quad, run_time=1.6)
stage.play(Create(marks))
stage.add(heavy, light, marks)

beats.intent: Gravity arrows: 100 N on the heavy ball, 10 N on the light one; each mass is that much harder to speed up
beats.narration: Gravity pulls the heavy ball ten times as hard, a hundred newtons against ten. But it also takes ten times the force to speed it up, so both speed up at the same rate.
beats.code:
fh = Arrow(heavy.get_center() + 0.4 * UP + 1.4 * UP, heavy.get_center() + 0.4 * UP, buff=0, color=RED)
fl = Arrow(light.get_center() + 0.2 * UP + 0.6 * UP, light.get_center() + 0.2 * UP, buff=0, color=RED)
stage.play(GrowArrow(fh), GrowArrow(fl))
stage.add(fh, fl)
stage.label(fh, "100 N", direction=LEFT, color=RED)
stage.label(fl, "10 N", direction=RIGHT, color=RED)

beats.intent: The picture beside a = F/m: 100/10 = 10/1 = 10 m/s², and d = 5t² = 20 m at t = 2
beats.narration: Acceleration is force over mass: ten metres per second squared for both. Distance fallen is five t squared, twenty metres at two seconds.

request: why can't you divide by zero?

beats.intent: 12 dots split into groups of 3: four groups
beats.narration: Twelve divided by three asks: how many threes make twelve? Four.
beats.code:
stage.title("Dividing by zero")
dots = VGroup(*[Dot([-5.6 + 0.5 * i, 1.0, 0], radius=0.12, color=BLUE) for i in range(12)])
stage.play(FadeIn(dots))
stage.add(dots)
groups = VGroup(*[SurroundingRectangle(VGroup(*dots[3 * g:3 * g + 3]), color=YELLOW, buff=0.1) for g in range(4)])
stage.play(Create(groups))
stage.add(groups)
stage.label(groups, "12 ÷ 3 = 4 groups", direction=DOWN, color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: Axes of group size against number of groups: 12 ÷ 3 = 4, 12 ÷ 2 = 6, 12 ÷ 1 = 12, 12 ÷ 0.5 = 24
beats.narration: Make the groups smaller and you need more of them: groups of two, six; groups of one, twelve; groups of a half, twenty four.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
ax = Axes(x_range=[0, 6, 1], y_range=[0, 30, 6], x_length=6, y_length=4.4, axis_config={"include_numbers": True}).move_to([-2.8, -0.6, 0])
stage.play(Create(ax))
stage.add(ax)
pts = VGroup(*[Dot(ax.c2p(x, 12 / x), color=YELLOW) for x in (3, 2, 1, 0.5)])
stage.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(p) for p in pts], lag_ratio=0.3))
stage.add(pts)
stage.play(FadeIn(Text("group size", font_size=24).next_to(ax.x_axis, DOWN, buff=0.45)), FadeIn(Text("groups", font_size=24).next_to(ax.y_axis, UP)))

beats.intent: The curve 12 ÷ x shooting up without bound as the group size shrinks to 0
beats.narration: As the group size shrinks towards zero, the number of groups grows without end. Groups of zero never add up to twelve, however many you take.
beats.code:
curve = ax.plot(lambda x: 12 / x, x_range=[0.42, 6], color=ORANGE)
stage.play(Create(curve))
stage.add(curve)
up = Arrow(ax.c2p(0.6, 22), ax.c2p(0.6, 30), buff=0, color=RED)
stage.play(GrowArrow(up))
stage.add(up)
stage.label(up, "no end", direction=RIGHT, color=RED)

beats.intent: The graph beside 3 × 4 = 12 but 0 × ? = 12 has no answer
beats.narration: Division undoes multiplication: twelve divided by three is four because three times four is twelve. Twelve divided by zero would need zero times something to be twelve, and nothing works.
